reasoning.complexity: O(decimal digit count) time and O(1) auxiliary storage; at most ten input digits.
reasoning.limitation: This is a source-visible bounded-integer argument, not a claim that CPython or JavaScript engine native storage/arithmetic use only32bits. JavaScript negativezero serializes as0; the integer problem does not distinguish them.
reasoning.mandatory_requirement: Every source-visible integral value is signed32: value is never abs(INT_MIN), the floor quotient is at least -214748365, corrected digit lies -9..0, accumulator multiplication occurs only when result>=-214748364, and the last-digit cutoff guarantees the addition stays above the sign-dependent minimum. Positive outputs cannot negate INT_MIN.
reasoning.numerical_behavior: Digits are consumed with truncation toward zero into a nonpositive accumulator. Python adjusts the floor divmod quotient/remainder when the remainder is nonzero; JavaScript truncates division directly. The final sign is restored only after an overflow-safe accumulation.

reasoning.mandatory_requirement: The solve AST has no binary Add/Sub, augmented Add/Sub, unary UAdd/USub. No helper uses them. Only bitwise xor,and,shift,complement and comparison are used for arithmetic.
reasoning.numerical_behavior: Masking realizes addition modulo2**32. The carry loop moves pending carries to higher bits and terminates within32rounds. Complement of x^MASK converts a negative signed result without subtraction. Legal input sums lie within[-2000,2000].

reasoning.complexity: O(n+k*log(n)) time, O(n) live auxiliary space. O(1) memory and O(n) time are optional followups and are not claimed.
reasoning.javascript_heap_invariants: Heapify establishes the min-heap property. An advanced row head is not smaller than its consumed head, so root replacement needs only down-sifting. An exhausted row is removed by moving the final heap record to root and down-sifting. The final single-element pop leaves an empty heap and skips assignment. Equal values are interchangeable but still individually consumed.
reasoning.limitation: Live-storage asymptotics do not measure a particular garbage collector peak. The upcoming frozen run must still enforce and report actual resource limits.
reasoning.mandatory_requirement: Python heapq.merge is lazy and retains O(n) row iterators/heap entries; star-expansion adds O(n) references. JavaScript has at most one three-element record per row and constant extra live references. Neither constructs an n*n intermediate.
reasoning.numerical_behavior: Each nonexhausted sorted row contributes one current head. Removing the minimum head and advancing only its row enumerates all values with multiplicity in nondecreasing order; the kth removed value is the answer.

reasoning.complexity: O(n) amortized time and O(1) auxiliary storage excluding returned output. Ascents can be charged to completed trie subtrees/previous descents; trailing9 ascents form a geometric total. The final unused cursor update is still bounded and terminates at zero before increment.
reasoning.limitation: This is an algorithmic source review, not a formal proof or measured all-input complexity certification.
reasoning.mandatory_requirement: The returned list is required output storage. Apart from it, only a fixed number of scalar variables are live; there is no sort, recursion, stack or auxiliary container.
reasoning.numerical_behavior: The scalar cursor follows decimal-trie preorder: descend to the zero child when available, otherwise ascend past exhausted suffixes and increment to the next sibling. This enumerates1..n exactly once in lexicographic order.
